source.title: Exploring OpenAI's Latent Directions: Tests, Observations, and Poking Around

record.tranche_reason: It qualitatively evaluates whether transformer neurons yield coherent or mixed concept activations, using interactive searches and top-activation matching rather than the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: The post reports neuron-search results for a red prompt and an Odyssey passage, including a qualitative polysemanticity example and per-layer matching counts. SAE-direction-only results are excluded because they do not measure the claim's target, individual neurons. The per-layer counts are counts of matching results, not counts of polysemantic neurons.
record.test_reason: An exploratory Neuronpedia search of GPT2-SMALL MLP neurons. It reports qualitatively that most top neuron results for an Odyssey passage were mismatched or highly polysemantic, which bears weakly on V2. The study's main aim is evaluating SAE directions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that SAE directions were consistently and significantly better than neurons at identifying concepts in a text, and that no monosemantic red neuron could be found. Direction quality declined in later layers, and neurons were relatively competitive in layers 6–9. The author calls neurons 'a disaster' but gives no prevalence estimate of polysemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: Interactive Neuronpedia searches and qualitative inspection of GPT2-SMALL neuron activations and SAE directions, rather than the original studies' neuron analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Neuron match counts for the Odyssey search varied across layers (17 in layer 0 and 3 in layers 10 and 11); the post does not report per-layer denominators.

fits_no_version.finding: For the red concept, the best candidate neuron 2:553 was a general color neuron and clearly worse than SAE direction 1-MLP-OAI:22004. No monosemantic red neuron was found.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE directions isolate specific concepts better than individual GPT2-SMALL neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-layer neuron token-match counts (17,14,14,7,8,9,17,14,13,13,3,3 for layers 0–11) are lower than SAE direction counts in every layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE directions match input-text concepts more often than neurons in every layer of GPT2-SMALL.

record.problems: The evaluation is exploratory and uses selected search results, one Odyssey passage, and a qualitative match criterion. Per-layer match denominators and uncertainty estimates are not reported; a lack of a matching top token does not itself establish polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: Direction-only outcomes and the direction match counts in the per-layer table were left out because they concern SAE directions, not individual neurons. Other qualitative direction examples and observations are likewise outside the claim's target.

untested.parts: The share of MLP neurons that are polysemantic and a layer-wise prevalence estimate. Only selected search results for one prompt were inspected qualitatively.
Reinterpretation of polysemantic neurons as one shared feature.
Dependence on activation range or scoring method.

missing.what: Of the four matching top neurons, the author says most also activated on unrelated tokens. This is direct qualitative evidence of polysemanticity among the matched neurons.
The author could not find a monosemantic red neuron in any layer; color neurons found were general color neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The study is weak evidence: an informal blog post with one prompt and a qualitative criterion. I removed the record's V2 limits_scope label because it described untested breadth, not a qualifying result; that breadth is now listed under untested. Tranche T2 is retained, though T3 is arguable.

versions.untested_parts: The study examines selected GPT2-SMALL search results for one text snippet, not a representative share of all MLP neurons or a systematic range of contexts.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure, including effects of initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Controlled comparisons of activation functions, architectures, or regularization, and performance costs.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons reveal a shared feature when examined with better tools.
A comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods for deciding whether a neuron is polysemantic.

rows.measure: Number of top neuron results whose activating tokens matched the passage's concepts or words.
rows.value: Four of the top 25 matched; the post says most did not have matching or similar activating tokens, or were highly polysemantic.

rows.check: The 4/25 match count measures token matching, not polysemanticity. Set state to observed on that statement. 'partial' did not reflect what the text says.
